Hi Priyom / Kimberly,

Thanks for the proposal packet — the team had a couple of follow-ups on the commercial section before we finalize the RFP response. High level asks:

- Can you confirm how commit phasing would work if we ramp usage across Q1–Q4? We want an option that lets us step into a larger commit mid-year without punitive pro-rating.
- How are overages priced once we exceed the committed tokens in a billing period? Is it a simple per-token surcharge or tiered?
- Do you offer any surge/burst protection (credits or a pooled cushion)? If so, how does it reconcile on the invoice and in a true-up?
- What is your true-up cadence (monthly/quarterly/annual) and do you support carry-forward credits for underspend?

We also need a worked example (pdf or spreadsheet) showing a 3-month spike and how credits / overages would be applied. Can you get that to us before next Wednesday? Procurement will use that to model TCO.

Attaching our RFP commercial worksheet for reference — please mark any assumptions.

Appreciate it — Jordan

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Outlined below is Redwood's standard commercial posture plus two alternative structures depending on how Skyborne prefers to manage risk and cashflow. I attached a concise Excel worked example (Skyborne_RFP_Comm_Summary.xlsx).

Summary (short):
- True-up cadence: Quarterly by default (monthly on request for pilots).
- Commit phasing: We support staged commits with mid-year step-ups. Additional commit takes effect pro-rata from the effective date with no back-charges for prior months.
- Overages: Default overage rate = 1.5x published committed unit price for the billing period. For large, predictable spikes we can apply a tiered overage (1.25x up to 150% of committed, 1.75x beyond).
- Burst protection: Offer an optional Burst Credit Pool (BCP) sized as a % of committed tokens. Credits are consumed first during the month, then overages billed if credits exhausted. Unused credits expire quarterly (or roll forward by agreement).
- Credits & carry-forward: Underspend can be converted to credits at invoice close and carried forward up to 2 quarters; custom longer carry-forward available with a multi-year commit.

Two commercial options (examples):
1) Commit + Burst Cushion (recommended for predictable growth)
   - Annual committed token ladder (e.g., 100M / 200M / 350M) with quarterly true-ups.
   - Burst Credit Pool = 10% of annual commit (applied on monthly basis).
   - Overages: 1.25x up to 150% of monthly commit, 1.75x beyond.
   - Pricing: step-up to larger commit mid-year prorated forward; no retroactive charge.

2) Metered with Volume Discounts (recommended for conservative starts)
   - Pay-as-you-go list rate, volume discount tiers applied monthly.
   - Optional capped burst cushion for the pilot quarter.
   - True-up monthly.

Next steps: Which structure should I model in the worked example? I'll also include a short invoice sample and a burst-credit worked example if you want the burst cushion flow.

Attachments: Skyborne_RFP_Comm_Summary.xlsx

Thanks — Priyom

Jordan — quick answers and the requested artifacts attached. Quoted your questions below for clarity.

> For the Burst Credit Pool (BCP): if we buy a BCP sized at X tokens and consume them across multiple months, does Redwood apply credits to the month where consumption occurred or at true-up only?

Short answer: Credits are applied to the month(s) of consumption. Operational detail: when a request consumes tokens, the serving runtime tags consumption to the customer's monthly usage ledger. If the monthly usage exceeds the committed tokens for that month, the system first deducts from any remaining BCP balance for that billing month. If BCP is exhausted, overage pricing is applied. At quarterly true-up we reconcile any remaining BCP balance (unused credits can roll forward up to two quarters by default).

> If we step up a commit mid-year and then subsequently drop usage, do you offer downgrade windows or is the new commit durable for the remainder of the term?

We support one downgrade window per 12-month period, with a 30-day notice and pro-rated adjustment effective at the next billing period. Downgrades are subject to a minimum-commit floor (typically 80% of the highest monthly run-rate in the prior quarter) unless an exception is negotiated.

> Can you provide a short SLA-credit table and sample invoice?

Attached: mutual_action_plan_v1.docx (action timeline + who's responsible), burst-credit-worked-example.pdf (3-month spike worked example), and a one-page sample invoice embedded in the Excel file we sent earlier. Quick SLA summary: 

- Availability < 99.9% and >= 99.0%: 5% service credit on monthly invoice.
- Availability < 99.0% and >= 95.0%: 15% credit.
- Availability < 95.0%: case-by-case remediation + possible termination rights after cure window.

Latency SLO (90th pct): credits tiered at 10% for >200ms degradation beyond target, escalating for repeated misses. Precise thresholds are contractible in the SOW.

Invoice mechanics: credits appear as line items next to the affected month (separate credit memo also issued for accounting). BCP consumption is shown as "Burst credits applied" rows; overages show unit price, quantity, and total surcharge. At quarterly true-up we produce a reconciliation statement showing net credits carried forward or additional overage charges.

If this matches what procurement needs, I'll fold these artifacts into the RFP appendix and send a redline-friendly commercial term sheet. Also proposing a short call Thursday 10am PT to walk procurement through the worked example.

Thanks — Priyom
